The tom-tom is a cylindrical membranophone without snares, with a head on one or both sides, its shell fitted with metal hoops, tension screws and mounts so that it can be clamped to the bass drum, put on a floor stand or carried on a marching harness; the floor tom of a drum kit is struck with drumsticks. It joined the drum kit at the beginning of the twentieth century and became the rack tom and floor tom of rock, fusion and other kit set-ups. Its name is connected with the Thammattama of the Sinhalese of Sri Lanka, which in Buddhist rites is played together with the reed-pipe horanava; the North American drum kit also developed a tunable version.
通通鼓為無響弦圓筒形膜鳴鼓，名稱來自英屬印度語與僧伽羅語，二十世紀初加入鼓組。前: The tom-tom is a snareless cylindrical membranophone whose name comes from Anglo-Indian and Sinhalese, and it joined the drum kit at the beginning of the twentieth century. Its forerunner can be traced to the Thammattama, used by the Sinhalese of Sri Lanka in Buddhist rites and often played in the monastery together with the reed-pipe horanava; British colonists' complaints about South Asian drumming may have helped the name enter the West. Early American drum kits mostly called them Chinese tom-toms, with pigskin heads tacked to a wooden shell. In 1936 the Slingerland company and Gene Krupa brought out a tension system that tunes the top and bottom heads, and the 13×9 inch rack tom and 16×16 inch floor tom became lasting standards; the one-rack-one-floor set-up was common in the 1950s and 1960s, single-headed concert toms appeared in the 1970s, and deeper power toms were popular in the 1980s.
通通鼓為無響弦的圓柱形膜鳴鼓，來源標示地區為美洲／北美，二十世紀初加入鼓組。其名: The tom-tom is a snareless cylindrical membranophone, with the Americas / North America given as its region, and it joined the drum kit at the beginning of the twentieth century. The Sri Lankan drum its name points to, the Thammattama, is found in Theravada Buddhist monastery rites and is played together with the reed-pipe horanava; in the modern drum kit it is used in rock, fusion and other set-ups, and there are variants such as concert toms, band toms and rototoms. Rototoms can be used by composers as pitched instruments; the source lists no particular works.
通通鼓為膜鳴圓筒鼓，鼓皮早期以豬皮釘於木殼，並用金屬釘固定；現代資料僅載有鼓皮，: The tom-tom is a membranous cylindrical drum; the head was once pigskin tacked to a wooden shell and held with metal tacks, and the modern sources record only the head, with the material not specified. The shell is usually six to eight plies of wood such as mahogany, falkata, birch or maple, and solid wood, fibreglass, pressed steel, acrylic and resin composites are also found. The hardware is chrome- or metal-plated, with metal or wooden hoops, tension rods, lugs and nut boxes. The rototom has no shell, only a head and a steel rim. The materials of the remaining parts are not stated.
通通鼓音色清脆明亮，具有良好的穿透力，能在樂隊中清晰突出。其音域居中偏高，隨鼓身: The tom-tom has a clear, bright timbre that carries well and stands out plainly in a band. Its range is in the middle and upper middle, varying with the size of the shell: a large tom is lower and warmer, a small one sharper. The tension of the head decides the quality — tighter means brighter and cleaner, slacker means heavier and darker. The way it resonates is unusual, both heads vibrating together, which gives it a natural decay. Beside the depth of the bass drum the tom-tom is more agile; beside the sharpness of the snare it is rounder and gentler. Its quick decay makes it especially good for fast rhythms and busy drum fills.
